why: Useful movement is not a contest between perfect form and maximum volume. The task, dose, goals, confidence, and individual response all matter.

slides.title: More Than Perfect Form
slides.content: There is often more than one acceptable way to move. Technique can matter for a task without one posture being mandatory for every body.

slides.title: Dose Matters Too
slides.content: Load, repetitions, speed, range, frequency, recovery, and current capacity can all influence how an activity is tolerated.

slides.title: Make It Meaningful
slides.content: Activities that connect to your goals and preferences may be easier to practise consistently. Adherence is part of a useful plan.

slides.title: Use Feedback, Not Fear
slides.content: Notice symptoms, confidence, function, and recovery after activity. Adjust thoughtfully rather than assuming every sensation means damage.

slides.title: Try This Today
slides.content: Choose one familiar exercise and a manageable dose. Note what felt controlled, what mattered to you, and what you would adjust next time.
